about: An XMLTV timestamp to Unix milliseconds, or null when it is not one.
notes: The stamp is local to the offset it carries, so the offset is subtracted to reach UTC.

With no offset the stamp is taken as UTC. That is a decision, not a reading of the spec: a guide that is silent about its zone is most often already in UTC, and guessing the viewer's zone would shift every programme by hours on a correct feed.

a stamp with a negative offset
no offset is taken as UTC
seconds are optional
cases.why: Plenty of feeds write only to the minute.

cases.name: an offset with a half hour
cases.why: India is +0530 and a half-hour error puts every programme in the wrong slot.

cases.name: a sentence is not a time
an ISO timestamp is not an XMLTV one
cases.why: Accepting it would be generous and wrong: the formats disagree about what the digits mean.
